newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - Akzo DSM profit seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Akzo DSM profit seen up.

text.p: Chemical firms DSM and Akzo Nobel are both seen posting higher first-half profits this week, aided by exchange rate effects and a buoyant industry cycle.
DSM is seen reporting first-half profit from ordinary operations of 452-544 million guilders on Tuesday, compared with a year-earlier 425 million.
"Everyone is agreed on the trend in profits, but the uncertainty lies in the degree of improvement," says Ab Barneveld, chemicals analyst with Generale Bank.
Consensus of DSM first-half ordinary earnings amounts to 250.1 million guilders.
The earnings rise will be mainly underpinned by improved margins at DSM's hydrocarbons and polymers activities as the effect of lower naphtha prices kicks in, analysts believe.
Dollar strength versus the guilder will also aid profits, they say.
Akzo Nobel is seen posting a rise in second quarter earnings from ordinary operations to 375-427 million guilders, with the consensus estimate at 405.7 million.
Akzo, whose more limited focus on bulk petrochemicals renders it less cyclical than DSM, posted ordinary profits of 367 million guilders in the second 1996 quarter.
Here too the rise is seen underpinned by the company's cyclical chemicals activities, which ING Barings' Quirijn Mulder sees picking up by some 20 percent.
"The earnings improvement will come particularly from the cyclical activities," Mulder says, adding operating income is seen up across all divisions.
Favourable currency exchange rates will also aid Akzo's earnings, translating faster into its bottom line than at DSM.
Barneveld agrees Akzo can look forward to a major year-on-year upturn in its base chemicals business.
Akzo's coatings business will also continue to improve, as lower raw material costs boost margins.

While start-up costs for new drugs Remeron and Puregon will pressure pharmaceuticals profits, this will be compensated by the performance of other units such as veterinary drugs subsidiary Intervet, analysts say.
Now the problems at man-made fibres have been contained, this segment should also show an improvement, they believe.
"I see fibres' contribution rising to 20 million from 15, but the unit will never amount to much," says Marina Millington of Bangert, Pontier and partners.
Akzo Nobel's second quarter net earnings will come in around 406 million guilders, a rise supported across all its divisions, she predicts.
